testsWritten: PayloadEstimateTest: 18 tests covering tokenEstimate/payloadSizeLabel/footerLabel for counts 0,1,2,3,12 plus PAYLOAD_FORMAT_VERSION, the leading-space unit and the literal U+00B7 middot

testRun.output: Verified independently by the orchestrator with --rerun: :presentation-feature-mirror:desktopTest 244 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped (+26 this wave); :presentation-core-ui:desktopTest 29 tests, 0 failures. Cross-target :build green for BOTH modules (includes compileTestKotlinIosArm64 and runs iosSimulatorArm64Test). PayloadEstimateTest 18/18 green.

implementation.summary: New internal core/payload/PayloadEstimate.kt: tokenEstimate (360 + count*140, FINAL heuristic, no tokenizer), payloadSizeLabel (oneDecimal(1.6 + count*0.12) + ' MB'), footerLabel ('frame.png · N crops · hierarchy.xml'), PAYLOAD_FORMAT_VERSION = 1. oneDecimal is hand-rolled on (value*10).roundToInt() — String.format is JVM-only and would break Kotlin/Native; it appears in this file only inside a KDoc line explaining why it is avoided. Rounds rather than truncates (count 3 -> '2.0 MB') and always emits the tenths digit (count 12 -> '3.0 MB').

issues: one unexplained iOS release-link failure, green on re-run

TAC-1's boundary clause was initially unmet: counts 0/1/2/12 have hundredths 0,2,4,4 so rounding and truncation never diverge. Orchestrator sent the test author back to add count 3 (1.96 -> 2.0 round vs 1.9 truncate) before freeze; a truncating implementation would otherwise have passed the whole suite.

troubleshooting.issue: Implementer could have weakened a frozen test to go green.
troubleshooting.resolution: Orchestrator verified: no test file modified (git status shows only the two new untracked test files), 18+8 @Test, zero backticks, zero @Ignore.

troubleshooting.issue: iosSimulatorArm64 linkReleaseFramework failed once with no diagnostic line under parallel release links.
troubleshooting.resolution: Passed unchanged on re-run; orchestrator could not reproduce. Treated as a Kotlin/Native linker flake, not a code defect. Logged as a Stage 7 reflection candidate.

troubleshooting.issue: core/stats/StatsFormatter.kt already has a private tenths-formatting trick; reusing it would mean widening its visibility across package boundaries for two lines.
troubleshooting.resolution: Kept a local private oneDecimal using the same technique. No shared helper introduced.
